problem: Visual encoders used for navigation (ImageNet/CLIP/self-supervised pre-training on single images) capture static-image semantics but lack the spatial relationships between views and the environment structure that navigation needs. Fine-tuning encoders inside the navigation policy is expensive and generalizes poorly because of scarce scenes.
motivation: Humans build cognitive maps from perspective views that track semantics, space and movement. A top-down semantic map is a compact source of objects, structure, free space, unexplored regions and agent transitions, and it is more complete than the partial online maps built during navigation. Transferring this information into a frozen egocentric encoder could help many navigation tasks and models without needing online mapping.
key_idea: Contrastively align an RGBD encoder's features for a pair of source/target egocentric views with the features of a top-down semantic map (built by Semantic MapNet along the shortest path between them), so that map knowledge is distilled into the egocentric visual representation.
insight: The contrastive Ego2-Map loss is the most useful objective. Alone it gives +3.1 SR / +3.3 SPL over the CLIP baseline with A_High, and ablating the map's semantics, open-space information or the target view hurts A_High. Data diversity matters: using 50% of environments hurts more than 50% of samples, and MP3D-only data is worse than the baseline. Initializing the map encoder from CLIP matters: swapping it for IN-21K lowers R2R-CE results even though the pre-training loss saturates equally, so CLIP semantics appear to be passed to the RGBD encoder through the map encoder. Angular-offset prediction alone is harmful.
method: RGBD ViT encoder: a ViT-B/16 initialized from CLIP takes RGB and depth through two separate conv layers, token-wise concatenation and a non-linear projection, giving one compact RGBD feature. It is frozen for downstream navigation.

Ego2-Map contrastive objective: positives pair the source and target views (Is, It) with a top-down semantic map M of the shortest path between them. Negatives come from other routes or environments. Two MLP heads and a symmetric InfoNCE loss with a learnable temperature are used.

Map encoder: a ViT-B/32 with the last three layers unfrozen encodes the semantic map. The maps come from an off-the-shelf Semantic MapNet run on RGBD along the path, with the path drawn as a gradient line and a 360° turn added at the target.
Angular offset prediction: an auxiliary MSE regression of the signed angular offset in [-π, π] between two views at the same position.
Explorable distance prediction: an auxiliary regression of the maximal forward distance to an obstacle, capped to 0.5–5.0 m, from a single RGBD image.
Data collection: 252,537 viewpoints from the first 800 HM3D training scenes, over 1M RGBD images, 500k view pairs and 500k (Is, It, M) triplets. Paths are within 7 m and follow shortest paths.

Downstream use: the encoder replaces the two ResNets in a CWP-VLN-BERT agent (A_High: panorama plus waypoint predictor; A_Low: egocentric views with 15° turns and 0.25 m steps) and in a DD-PPO GRU ObjNav baseline.

setting.backbone: ViT-B/16 RGBD encoder (CLIP init, pre-trained with Ego2-Map, then frozen) + VLN-BERT / CWP agent (trained) for R2R-CE; GRU policy trained with DD-PPO for ObjNav
setting.training_data: Encoder: 500k view-pair/map triplets from 800 HM3D scenes (over 1M rendered RGBD images), starting from CLIP weights. Semantic MapNet was trained on MP3D. Agent: standard R2R-CE training data for VLN-BERT/CWP; ObjNav: original DD-PPO training data.
setting.observation: RGB + depth egocentric views (36-view panorama for A_High, single egocentric view for A_Low); ObjNav also uses GPS+compass
setting.action_space: A_High: candidate waypoints from a waypoint predictor; A_Low: low-level Turn Left/Right 15°, Forward 0.25 m, Stop
setting.simulator: Habitat (HM3D for pre-training; MP3D scenes for R2R-CE and ObjNav)
setting.privileged: none at test time (GT semantic maps are used only in pre-training, produced by Semantic MapNet from simulator RGBD and poses)

results: With the CWP-VLN BERT agent, Ego2-Map reaches 47% SR / 41% SPL on the R2R-CE test server, beating the previous best Sim2Sim (44 SR / 37 SPL). It improves over the CLIP baseline by +3.56 SPL (A_High) and +5.10 SPL (A_Low) on val-unseen. On MP3D ObjNav it gets 29.0 SR / 10.6 SPL with a frozen encoder, above OVRL (28.6 / 7.4), which was trained on OSD and fine-tuned end-to-end.
limitations: Needs semantic maps for pre-training, which requires semantic annotations or traversable scenes plus a generalizable semantic map constructor, so data collection is costly.
Angular-offset and explorable-distance objectives give inconsistent gains, and agents in A_Low remain far below A_High. The map encoder and the choice of map representation are left unexplored.
